summary: Torkel Brekke is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Oslo and earned a DPhil at Oxford under Richard Gombrich. He held posts at PRIO, Oslo Metropolitan University, and MF Norwegian School of Theology.

Toru Funayama works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner. His academic posts include associate professor at Kyushu University (attested 1999–2003) and professor at Kyoto University (attested 1995–2019).

Toru Haneda was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, he served Kyoto University as professor, dean, and director, and later headed the Institute of Eastern Culture and Toho Gakkai.

Toru Kumeji works in Buddhist studies and computational fields. He has held posts at the Center for Open Humanities Data and served as chief researcher at the Humanities Information Studies Institute (attested 2015).

Toru Sagara was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1946–1949). He later held posts at Ibaraki University (~1956–1967), the University of Tokyo (~1967–1982), and Kyoritsu Women's University (~1982–1992).

Toru Takahashi was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Keijo Imperial University (1926–1940), Fukuoka University (1949), and Tenri University (1950–1964).

Toru Tomabechi is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne. He held posts at Lausanne, the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and the Center for Open Humanities Data.
Toshiaki Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Toyo University and later held a post there.

Toshifumi Goto is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1982. He has held professorships at Tohoku University (attested 2003–2005) and Osaka University.
Toshihide Unebe is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under Issai Funahashi and served as a professor at Doho University (attested 1991).

Toshihiko Izutsu worked in philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. After studying at Keio University, he served as a professor there (1954–1981), and held later posts at McGill University (1969–1975) and the Iranian Institute of Philosophy (1975–1979).

Toshihiko Kimura specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1963) and held posts at Tohoku University, Tokai Gakuin University (attested 1981–1987), and Shitennoji University (attested 2015).
Toshihiro Wada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981 and served as a professor at Nagoya University (~1986–2020).

Toshiichi Endo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of Kelaniya and a doctoral degree at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under Mahinda Palihawadana and W. S. Karunatillake.

Toshikazu Watanabe works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held a research post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2011–2015) and became a professor at Kokugakuin University in 2018.

Toshiki Osada specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Hokkaido University (~1973–1977) and held positions at Kyoto University of the Arts (~1991–2003) and the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (~2003–2020).

Toshinori Ochiai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He held posts at Kacho Junior College (~1983–1996), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2018), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1996–2018).
Toshio Ando was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1929–1932) and held academic posts at Doho University (~1950–1954) and Otani University (~1954–1973).

Toshio Horiuchi works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Tokyo (~2002–2009) and held research positions at Toyo University (~2009–2017) and Zhejiang University (~2017).

Toshio Nagahiro was a scholar of history, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University, he served there as a researcher, associate professor, and professor (~1953–1969), and later was president of Kyoto Tachibana University (1978–1986).
